messages:
sasha: heads-up — canary for cobalt14b int4 with the new prefetch+warmup policy is spiking mem around step ~4k and we see a small QA/regression vs fp16 baseline. canary id canary-4872. logs below, any ideas?

sasha: ```
[2026-03-19 14:02:11] worker-7 mem: 14.9G resident, alloc fail retries=3
[2026-03-19 14:02:12] kv_cache resize triggered, slot_alloc fail, fallback sync
[2026-03-19 14:02:13] generation: seq_len=1024 window=2048 prefetch=2 warmup=6
```

sasha: config snippet: ```
model: cobalt14b-int4
quant: qtk-v1.3
batching: dynamic
batch_ms: 8
max_generation_window: 2048
prefetch: true
prefetch_size: 2
warmup_steps: 6
slot_reserve: false
```

rodney: thanks. pinging @lia for kv-cache / alloc pattern look. also what's the steady batch size distribution? 

lia: I can take a look. initial thought: warmup_steps=6 might be repeatedly allocating big attention buffers then freeing which fragments memory under jemalloc. do you see lots of small frees in the logs?

sasha: not many small frees, more large alloc/free churn when the window slides. batch percentiles: p50=1, p95=3, p99=6. most requests are short but occasional long ones trigger the window.

ciara: sounds like fragmentation + int4 transient buffers. two quick experiments that usually help: enable slot_reserve (reserve a small slab for attention KV), or reduce warmup to 1 and switch to reclaim-friendly allocator flags. also try `aligned_tensor_alloc=true` in runtime to avoid mixed-size allocs.

rodney: +1. also try toggling prefetch_size from 2 -> 1 and see if that smooths allocations; prefetch can create duplicate large tensors for overlapping windows.

lia: another angle: keep prefetch but change prefetch_policy to "lazy" so it only allocs when next tokens are requested rather than up-front. that reduces peak but keeps latency win for steady streams.

sasha: ok running two quick canaries now: (A) warmup_steps=1, slot_reserve=true, prefetch_size=1; (B) aligned_alloc=true, prefetch_policy=lazy. will post numbers in ~20m.

deploy-bot: canary-4872 -> created. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/canaries/canary-4872 (status: running) :rocket:

sasha: quick interim: A reduced peak mem from ~14.9G -> ~12.7G on worker-7 and eliminated the slot_alloc fail line. latency p95 unchanged, QA delta narrowed from -1.8% to -0.2%.

lia: nice. that strongly points at warmup/prefetch causing the fragmentation. recommend we default cobalt14b-int4 to warmup_steps=1 + slot_reserve=true and prefetch_size=1 for now. we should add an opt-in lazy-prefetch flag for Dedicated customers with low P95 SLOs.

ciara: agreed. also file a small follow-up to test jemalloc tunables vs tcmalloc; int4 allocation patterns can vary. I'll open a short ticket.

rodney: SG. sasha, once you confirm B results we can roll the config change to the canary template and mark as mitigated.

sasha: B also looks good: aligned_alloc=true + lazy prefetch cut peak to 12.9G and QA delta to +0.1% (within noise). will push config change to canary template and create PR for default onboarding overrides.

deploy-bot: canary-4872 -> updated status: healthy. roll plan suggested by @lia queued as pr#5823.

sasha: thanks team. next steps: PR #5823 (default cobalt14b-int4 runtime overrides), ticket INF-2947 to benchmark jemalloc vs tcmalloc for int4 traces, and add a quicknote in model-onboarding checklist to run fragmentation smoke tests.
